threepl.exec

Class PipeRefs

  • java.lang.Object
    • threepl.exec.PipeRefs
  • All Implemented Interfaces:
    TDEConstants, Constant

    public class PipeRefs
extends java.lang.Object
implements Constant, TDEConstants
    This class represents a collection of pipe references. It is used in the generation of pipe acknowledgements. Pipe availability may be conditional on a signal; the test operand for a ?: operator or a selection input to a select() function.

    Field 'write_pipes' is a (possibly empty) set containing the pipe variables (Var) whose write availability is required. This is used by sync{}. Field 'read_pipes' is a (possibly empty) set containing the pipe variables (Var) whose read availability is required. This is used by sync{}.

    Field 'read_ands' is a set of pipes and conditional signals which are all to be used to form availability and acknowledge expressions. This field is a set of set pairs, the pair being a pipe variable set and a conditional signal set. For each set entry the pipe and signal sets are all ANDed together to form one term. The terms for each position in the lists are ORed together. Sets are used for the pipes and signals to be ANDed to avoid duplicate entries.

    When a write pipe is ANDed to this pipe reference by method 'and_set' it is added to the 'write_pipes' set.

    When a read pipe is ANDed to this pipe reference by method 'and_set' it is added to the 'read_pipes' set. If set 'read_ands' is empty the pipe is added as a new pair otherwise it is added to every pipe set in list 'read_ands'.

    When a conditional signal is ANDed to this pipe reference by method 'and' it is added to every signal set in list 'read_ands'.

    When another pipe reference is ANDed to this pipe reference by method 'and_set', if this pipe reference 'read_ands' set is not empty the product of the two pipe references is generated by taking each combination of list indices from each pipe reference and taking a union of the sets. If this pipe reference 'read_ands' set is empty the pipe reference is copied.

    When another pipe reference is ORed to this pipe reference by method 'or' the lists are appended.

    This process of multiplying through each time means that we maintain the pipe dependencies as a sum of products, no deeper.

      • setReadAVCheck

        public void setReadAVCheck(PipeRefs pr)
        Set the read availability check set from a pipes reference. The set will be empty prior to this - this method is only called at one place in nodes/ExprNode.java when evaluating the pipe read availability operator and the class is newly constructed prior to the call. Pipes from both the argument write availability check set and the argument write pipes set are added.
        Parameters:
        pr - is the pipes reference

      • getSyncAvail

        public Val getSyncAvail(Scope module_scope,
                        PipeRefs checkedpipes,
                        SrcLoc loc)
        Get the sync block availability signal for this pipes reference, or null. If there are no pipe references null is returned. Note that the pipe availability does not include any conditional signals (from pipes in the 2nd or 3rd arguments of a ?: operator). This is only called from one place in method syncAvail in exec/Pipe.java which in turn is only called in one place in nodes/SyncBlock.java.
        Parameters:
        module_scope - is the scope we are in
        checkedpipes - lists pipes that need not be checked for availability
        loc - is the source file location
        Returns:
        the availability value

        Add the acknowledgement logic for the pipes referenced in this pipe reference.
        Parameters:

        exec - is the push or pop signal for the pipe

        loc - is the source file location

      • unbufferedPipes

        public boolean unbufferedPipes(boolean allow_one,
                               java.lang.String mess,
                               SrcLoc loc)
        Examine an instance of the class for pipes of zero depth, i.e. unbuffered. If there are no unbuffered pipes then false is returned. If allow_one is true and there is a single unbuffered pipe then true is returned. If allow_one is true and there is more than one unbuffered pipe an exception is thrown using the message argument.
        Parameters:
        allow_one - if true directs that one unbuffered pipe is allowed
        mess - is an error message string
        loc - is a source file location
        Returns:
        true if there is an unbuffered pipe and it is allowed
